safety_verdicts.content: Her normal bowel habit is once per day.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state baseline bowel habit of once per day.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the patient’s baseline bowel frequency (normally once daily) slightly reduces the clinician’s ability to gauge deviation from baseline and recovery trajectory. It is unlikely to change acute management of presumed gastroenteritis.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient’s mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact with her.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention mother having similar symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document an additional close contact with similar symptoms could reduce recognition of a contagious outbreak and influence counseling/testing decisions. In most cases it would not materially change immediate dehydration-focused management.

Not recording “no rash” slightly weakens the review for systemic/infectious or allergic etiologies, but rash is not central to the presented diarrheal illness. This omission is unlikely to alter treatment or disposition.

safety_verdicts.content: No previous abdominal problems or surgery
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript supports no prior abdominal pains/problems but does not clearly confirm 'no surgery'; generated adds 'no surgery' without support.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Adding “no surgery” without support could falsely reassure clinicians and bias away from considering prior surgical complications (e.g., adhesions) when evaluating abdominal pain/vomiting. In this diarrheal illness context, the likelihood of significant harm is low but not zero.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript/gold do not state regular menstrual cycles; only LMP timing and menstrual cramps mentioned.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “regular menstrual cycles” without evidence can mislead reproductive history assessment and potentially reduce attention to menstrual irregularity as a symptom. It is unlikely to change management in this case but is clinically inaccurate.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold/transcript indicate 'no regular sexual intercourse' rather than 'not sexually active' (stronger claim not supported).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Recording “not sexually active” is a stronger claim than “no regular sexual intercourse” and could inappropriately lower suspicion for pregnancy-related causes of abdominal pain/vomiting or reduce consideration of pregnancy testing. This could plausibly delay diagnosis of pregnancy-related conditions in some scenarios.
